vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability is an arithmetic underflow in the unlock() function. The _lockedAmount state variable is not properly updated in transferFromWithLock() (missing assignment: _lockedAmount = _lockedAmount.add(_amount)). This causes _lockedAmount to remain 0 even after locking tokens. When unlock() is called, it attempts to subtract unlocked tokens from _lockedAmount (0 - X), causing an underflow that wraps _lockedAmount to a huge value (~2^256 - X). This huge value then bypasses the liquidity calculation in _transfer(), allowing attackers to drain contract tokens.
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate a whitelist admin to call lock functions. 2. Lock tokens using transferFromWithLock() (which doesn't update _lockedAmount). 3. Wait for lock period to expire. 4. Call unlock() to trigger underflow and get _lockedAmount set to huge value. 5. Exploit the broken liquidity calculation to drain contract tokens.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank() to impersonate a whitelist admin. 2. Use deal() to give attacker PLENTYCOIN tokens. 3. Approve contract to spend attacker's tokens. 4. Call transferFromWithLock() to lock tokens to attacker address. 5. Use vm.warp() to advance time past lock period. 6. Call unlock() to trigger underflow. 7. Verify _lockedAmount is now huge. 8. Transfer tokens from contract to drain funds.
